title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 14
statement: Given the nine-sided regular polygon \(A_1 A_2 A_3 A_4 A_5 A_6 A_7 A_8 A_9,\) how many distinct equilateral triangles in the plane of the polygon have at least two vertices in the set \(\{A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_9\}?\)

solutions.text:
Each of the \(\binom{9}{2} = 36\) pairs of vertices is a side of exactly two equilateral triangles, giving \(72\) triangles counted with multiplicity.

The triangles \(A_1 A_4 A_7,\) \(A_2 A_5 A_8,\) and \(A_3 A_6 A_9\) have all three vertices in the set, so each is counted three times instead of once, an overcount of \(2\) apiece.

The number of distinct triangles is \(72 - 3 \cdot 2 = 66.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Each pair of vertices is a side of exactly two equilateral triangles
This counts \(2\binom{9}{2}\) triangles, but the three all-vertex triangles get counted three times each
